newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Latam ADRs firm, market mulls Russia.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Latam ADRs firm, market mulls Russia.

text.p: Shares in Latin American companies firmed in New York on Thursday and traders weighed the potential effect of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's firing of his security adviser.
The market in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) also was following the larger rise in U.S. exchanges, traders and analysts said.

"Almost all the Mexican ADRs are up across the board," one trader said, bolstered by news of a stronger peso. After a recent fall, the same-day peso closed five centavos firmer due to pre-weekend swaps and an influx of dollars.
Among Mexican stocks, Telefonos de Mexico was up 3/8 to 31-5/8 on 1.19 million shares and Grupo Televisa rose 1/2 to 26-5/8.

Argentine shares also firmed as political uncertainty stemming from corruption allegations against some cabinet members faded. Telecom Argentina rose 5/8 to 38-5/8 and Telefonica de Argentina was up 3/8 to 23-3/4.
Traders also were watching developments in Russia, where Yeltsin dismissed security chief Alexander Lebed amid allegations he was plotting to set up his own security force in a bid to seize power.
The Templeton Russia Fund Inc was off 3/8 to 20-7/8. The Morgan Stanley Russia & New Europe Fund Inc was unchanged at 19-5/8.
"It's clear that the market does not how to deal with this sacking," said Serge Selfslagh, an investment manager for LGT Asset Management in London.
It was not immediately clear how the uncertainty might affect the upcoming private placement of shares in Russia's state-run RAO Gazprom GAZP.RTS, one of the world's biggest natural gas producers.
The placement will preface Gazprom's designation as a Level One ADR, where it will trade over the counter in the "pink sheets," the daily publication of the National Quotation Bureau.
Among European ADRs, the Netherlands' SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV was up 4-3/4 to 54 an a jump in third-quarter earnings.
British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc was up 1/8 to 63-1/4 on talk of linkups and interest in communications and broadcasting stocks.

Shares in Sweden's Toolex-Alpha NV, a maker of systems for production of compact discs, were off 5-5/8 to 12-3/8. The plummet followed a warning by the company that revenues for the first nine months of the year would be below its expectations.
In the early afternoon 138 of the 441 ADRs had advanced and 123 declined. Volume was 36.4 million shares.
